newsitem.title: UK: US firms to buy Yorkshire Electricity.
newsitem.headline: US firms to buy Yorkshire Electricity.

text.p: Britain's Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc said on Monday it had agreed to a 1.5 billion pound ($2.43 billion) cash offer from a company owned by American Electric Power Co Inc and Public Service Co of Colorado.
Yorkshire said the offer by Yorkshire Holdings valued its shares at 927 pence each in cash.

Yorkshire, which had been one of Britain's last remaining independent regional electricity companies, said the offer represented a premium of 13.3 percent to its closing price of 818.5 pence per share on Friday.
The bid was made at a multiple of 11.3 times Yorkshire's earnings per share, before exceptional items, for the year ended March 31, 1996.
The current Yorkshire Electricity management team will continue in their roles after the deal, the companies said.

"We can both add to Yorkshire Electricity's aspirations in the UK. We can also learn valuable skills and, together, look at other opportunities in the UK and further afield," AEP and PS Colorado said in a joint statement.
The companies said Yorkshire Electricity shareholders would retain the right to receive the interim dividend of 15.80 pence net per share.
AEP and PS Colorado serve over five million customers between them across nine U.S. states. ($1=.6168 Pound)
